literal: Chengzu, Emperor Wen, styled Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety — taboo name Di — was the fourth son of Taizu.
idiomatic: Chengzu, the Emperor Wen, whose posthumous titles ran through Opener of Heaven, Broadener of the Way, Lofty and Bright, Founder of the Fortune, Sacred in Martial Valor and Divine in Achievement, Pure in Benevolence and Supreme in Filial Piety, bore the personal name Di and was the fourth son of the dynastic founder.

literal: His mother was the Empress Xiaoci Gao.
idiomatic: His mother was Empress Ma, posthumously honored as the Xiaoci Gao Empress.

literal: In the third year of Hongwu he was enfeoffed as Prince of Yan.
idiomatic: In Hongwu year 3 he received the title Prince of Yan.

literal: In the thirteenth year he went to his fief at Beiping.
idiomatic: In year 13 he took up residence in his apanage at Beiping.

literal: The Prince's appearance was singularly imposing; his beard and mustache were handsome.
idiomatic: The Prince was striking in stature, with a fine beard and mustache.

literal: Wise and brave, possessed of great strategic vision, he could employ men by extending sincere trust.
idiomatic: He combined wisdom and courage with far-reaching design, and won service by treating men with open sincerity.

literal: In the twenty-third year, together with the Prince of Jin he campaigned against Nayir Buqa.
idiomatic: In year 23 he joined the Prince of Jin in a campaign against Nayir Buqa.

literal: The Prince of Jin was timid and dared not advance; the Prince doubled his march to Yidu Mountain, took the entire enemy force, and returned. Taizu was greatly pleased. Thereafter he repeatedly led the generals on campaign and was also ordered to command the border troops and horses along the frontier. The Prince's renown greatly increased.
idiomatic: The Prince of Jin hung back in fear, but the Prince of Yan forced the march to Mount Yidu, captured the whole enemy host, and returned in triumph. Taizu was delighted. After that he often led the generals in the field and was given authority over frontier soldiers and horses; his name resounded along the border.

literal: In the seventh month, on the day guiyou, he hid stalwart men at the Gate of Courteous Rites, lured Gui and Bing inside, killed them, and seized the Nine Gates.
idiomatic: On guiyou in the seventh month he concealed picked warriors at the Gate of Courteous Rites, drew in Zhang Bing and Xie Gui, killed them, and took the Nine Gates.

literal: He sent up a memorial to the Son of Heaven, denouncing Tai and Zicheng as treacherous ministers, and citing the Ancestral Instructions: "When the court lacks upright ministers and evil men arise within, the imperial princes shall drill their troops and await orders; the Son of Heaven will secretly instruct the princes to lead the garrison forces and suppress them."
idiomatic: He memorialized the throne, naming Qi Tai and Huang Zicheng as traitors and invoking the Ancestral Instructions: when the court has no upright ministers and villains stir within, imperial princes are to ready their troops and await command, and the Son of Heaven will secretly order the princes to lead frontier forces and put the rebellion down.

literal: Once the memorial had been sent, he raised his army.
idiomatic: The memorial dispatched, he took up arms.

literal: He appointed his own officials and styled his army the "Pacification of Difficulties."
idiomatic: He set up his own staff and called his host the Army of Pacifying the Realm's Troubles.

literal: He took Juyong Pass, broke Huailai, seized Song Zhong, captured Miyun, took Zunhua, and received the surrender of Yongping.
idiomatic: He carried Juyong Pass, stormed Huailai, took Song Zhong prisoner, seized Miyun, captured Zunhua, and won Yongping over.

literal: Within twenty days his forces reached several tens of thousands.
idiomatic: In twenty days his following swelled to tens of thousands.

literal: In the eighth month the Son of Heaven appointed Geng Bingwen grand general and sent him to campaign against the Prince.
idiomatic: In the eighth month the court named Geng Bingwen grand general and marched him against the Prince.

literal: On the day jiyou the army reached Zhending; the vanguard reached Xiong County.
idiomatic: On jiyou the main force reached Zhending while the van pressed to Xiong County.

literal: On the day renzi the Prince crossed the Baigou River by night, besieged Xiong, took the city, and put it to the sword.
idiomatic: On renzi the Prince forded the Baigou by night, invested Xiong, stormed it, and slaughtered the garrison.

literal: On the day jiayin the commanders-in-chief Pan Zhong and Yang Song came from Mozhou to relieve the city; ambush troops seized them, and the Prince then held Mozhou and returned to camp on the Baigou.
idiomatic: On jiayin the commanders Pan Zhong and Yang Song marched from Mozhou to the rescue; the Prince's ambush took them, and he seized Mozhou before withdrawing to the Baigou.

literal: Zhang Bao, a junior officer of the grand general, came over and reported that the grand general's army numbered three hundred thousand, of whom one hundred thirty thousand had arrived first — half encamped south of the Hutuo River and half north of it.
idiomatic: Zhang Bao, a staff officer under Geng Bingwen, defected and said the grand general had three hundred thousand men, with one hundred thirty thousand already up — half south of the Hutuo and half on the north bank.

literal: The Prince feared fighting the northern army while the southern army might take advantage; he therefore released Bao to return and had him spread word that the Prince's main force was about to arrive, luring the enemy to cross the river entirely to the north.
idiomatic: Fearing a clash with the northern wing while the southerners exploited his flank, the Prince sent Bao back with a story that the Prince's main body was closing in, drawing the whole enemy host across to the north bank.

literal: On the day renxu the Prince reached Zhending; with Zhang Yu, Tan Yuan, and others he attacked Bingwen's army from both sides, routed it utterly, and captured his lieutenant generals Li Jian and Ning Zhong and the regional commander Gu Cheng; heads taken numbered thirty thousand.
idiomatic: On renxu he came to Zhending and, with Zhang Yu and Tan Yuan, caught Geng Bingwen in a pincer, broke him completely, and took his deputies Li Jian and Ning Zhong and the regional commander Gu Cheng; thirty thousand heads were counted.

literal: He pressed the siege of Zhending; after two days it did not fall, and he withdrew.
idiomatic: He invested Zhending for two days without success, then drew off.

literal: When the Son of Heaven heard of Bingwen's defeat, he sent the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, to replace him in command of the army.
idiomatic: Learning of Geng Bingwen's rout, the court sent the Duke of Cao, Li Jinglong, to take over the army.

literal: In the ninth month, on the day wuchen, the Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, invested Yongping with Liaodong troops.
idiomatic: On wuchen in the ninth month the Marquis of Jiangyin, Wu Gao, laid siege to Yongping with troops from Liaodong.

literal: On the day wuyin Jinglong united five hundred thousand men and advanced to encamp at Hejian.
idiomatic: On wuyin Li Jinglong massed five hundred thousand men and moved to camp at Hejian.

literal: The Prince told his generals: "Jinglong looks fierce but is hollow within. Hearing that I am here he will not dare come at once. Better to go relieve Yongping and draw him out.
idiomatic: The Prince told his commanders, "Jinglong blusters but his heart fails him. While he knows I am here he will not rush forward — we should relieve Yongping and pull him after us.

literal: Wu Gao is timid and unfit for battle; when I arrive he is sure to flee; then we can turn and strike Jinglong.
idiomatic: Wu Gao is a coward and no fighter; once I appear he will run, and then we can wheel back on Jinglong.

literal: With a strong city before him and a great army behind, he is sure to be taken."
idiomatic: A walled city in front and a great host behind — he will be ours."

literal: On the day bingxu the Yan army marched to relieve Yongping.
idiomatic: On bingxu the Yan host set out for Yongping.

literal: On the day renchen, when Wu Gao heard the Prince had come, he indeed fled; the Prince pursued and defeated him.
idiomatic: On renchen Wu Gao, hearing the Prince was near, fled as foretold; the Prince chased him down and broke his force.

literal: He then pressed north toward Da Ning.
idiomatic: He then drove north toward Da Ning.

literal: On the day renyin he entered the city by stratagem.
idiomatic: On renyin he gained the city by ruse.

literal: After seven days he compelled the Prince of Ning, Quan, took the troops of Da Ning and the soldiers of the three guards of the Tumed, and all marched south together.
idiomatic: Seven days on he coerced the Prince of Ning, Quan, and marched south with the Da Ning host and the warriors of the three Tumed guards.

literal: On the day yimao he reached Huizhou and for the first time established the Five Armies.
idiomatic: On yimao he reached Huizhou and first organized the Five Armies.

literal: Zhang Yu commanded the center army, with Zheng Heng and He Shou as his deputies;
idiomatic: Zhang Yu led the center, with Zheng Heng and He Shou as deputies;

literal: Zhu Neng commanded the left army, with Zhu Rong and Li Jun as his deputies;
idiomatic: Zhu Neng led the left, with Zhu Rong and Li Jun as deputies;

literal: Li Bin commanded the right army, with Xu Li and Meng Shan as his deputies;
idiomatic: Li Bin led the right, with Xu Li and Meng Shan as deputies;

literal: Xu Zhong commanded the forward army, with Chen Wen and Wu Da as his deputies;
idiomatic: Xu Zhong led the van, with Chen Wen and Wu Da as deputies;

literal: Fang Kuan commanded the rear army, with He Yunzhong and Mao Zheng as his deputies.
idiomatic: Fang Kuan led the rear, with He Yunzhong and Mao Zheng as deputies.

literal: On the day dingsi he entered Songting Pass.
idiomatic: On dingsi he passed through Songting Pass.

literal: When Jinglong heard the Prince had gone to Da Ning, he indeed led his army to besiege Beiping, built ramparts at the Nine Gates, and the heir apparent held firm without giving battle.
idiomatic: Li Jinglong, learning the Prince had gone to Da Ning, did invest Beiping, threw up works at the Nine Gates, and the heir apparent held the walls without fighting.

literal: In the eleventh month, on the day gengwu, the Prince halted at Gushan.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on gengwu, the Prince made camp at Gushan.

literal: Scouts returned and reported that the Bai River's ice was breaking up and could not be crossed.
idiomatic: Patrols came back saying the ice on the Bai River was breaking and the crossing was impossible.

literal: The Prince prayed to the spirits; when he arrived the ice had joined solid, and he crossed his army.
idiomatic: The Prince prayed; when he reached the river the floes had knit into a road, and he took his army across.

literal: Jinglong sent the regional commander Chen Hui to reconnoiter the enemy; he took the left road and came out behind the Prince's army.
idiomatic: Li Jinglong sent the regional commander Chen Hui to scout; Chen took the left track and fell in behind the Prince's line.

literal: The Prince divided his force to strike back; Hui's men scrambled to cross the river, the ice suddenly broke apart, and countless drowned.
idiomatic: The Prince split off a detachment to hit him from behind; Chen Hui's men rushed the river, the ice gave way, and the drowned were beyond counting.

literal: On the day xinwei he fought Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.
idiomatic: On xinwei he met Li Jinglong at Zhengcun Dam.

literal: The Prince with picked cavalry first broke seven of his camps; the other generals followed, Jinglong was utterly defeated and fled back.
idiomatic: With elite horsemen he shattered seven camps in succession; the other commanders piled on, Li Jinglong was routed, and fled.

literal: On the day yihai he again sent up a memorial pleading his own case.
idiomatic: On yihai he again memorialized the throne in his own defense.

literal: In the twelfth month Jinglong redeployed his troops at Dezhou, planning a great advance in the coming spring.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month Li Jinglong regrouped at Dezhou, intending a major campaign the next spring.

literal: The Prince then planned to strike Datong, saying: "If we attack Datong they are sure to hurry to its relief. Datong is bitterly cold; the southern troops are frail, and they will be worn down without fighting."
idiomatic: The Prince turned toward Datong, saying, "Strike Datong and they must march to save it — a land of killing cold where southern soldiers wilt before they even fight."

literal: On the day gengshen he received the surrender of Guangchang.
idiomatic: On gengshen Guangchang submitted.

literal: In the first month of the second year, on the day bingyin, he took Weizhou.
idiomatic: In spring of year 2, on bingyin in the first month, he captured Weizhou.

literal: In the second month, on the day guichou, he reached Datong.
idiomatic: In the second month, on guichou, he arrived at Datong.

literal: Jinglong indeed came by the Zijing Pass to relieve it.
idiomatic: Li Jinglong, as expected, came through Zijing Pass to relieve the city.

literal: The Prince had already wheeled his army back to Juyong; many of Jinglong's troops died of cold and hunger, and seeing no enemy he returned.
idiomatic: The Prince had already swung back to Juyong; Li Jinglong's men froze and starved by the thousands, found no foe, and trudged home.

literal: In the fourth month of summer Jinglong advanced on Hejian; he and Guo Ying, Wu Jie, and Ping An arranged to meet at the Baigou River.
idiomatic: In the fourth month Li Jinglong pushed on Hejian and arranged with Guo Ying, Wu Jie, and Ping An to join at the Baigou.

literal: On the day yimao the Prince encamped at Sujia Bridge.
idiomatic: On yimao the Prince camped at Sujia Bridge.

literal: On the day jiwei he encountered Ping An's troops on the riverbank.
idiomatic: On jiwei he ran into Ping An's force on the river flats.

literal: The Prince rode forward with a hundred horsemen, feigned retreat, lured An's formation into movement, and struck when it did; An was defeated and fled.
idiomatic: The Prince led a hundred riders forward, pretended to flee, drew Ping An's line into disorder, and charged; Ping An broke and ran.

literal: He then pressed close on Jinglong's army; the battle went ill.
idiomatic: He closed on Li Jinglong's host, but the fight turned against him.

literal: At dusk he gathered his troops; the Prince with three horsemen brought up the rear. By night he lost the road, dismounted, lay on the ground to watch the stream, and so distinguished east from west, crossed the river, and departed.
idiomatic: At dusk he drew in his men; the Prince himself rearguarded with three riders. Night found him off the track; he dismounted, pressed his ear to the water to read its flow, found east from west, forded, and escaped.

literal: On the day gengshen he fought again.
idiomatic: On gengshen battle was joined again.

literal: Jinglong drew up his line for tens of li and broke the Yan rear guard.
idiomatic: Li Jinglong's battle line stretched for tens of li and shattered the Yan rear.

literal: The Prince himself led picked cavalry in a lateral strike and cut down Qu Neng, father and son.
idiomatic: The Prince led picked cavalry in a flanking blow and killed Qu Neng and his son.

literal: He ordered Qiu Fu to pierce the center but he could not break through.
idiomatic: He sent Qiu Fu to punch the center, but Qiu Fu could not break in.

literal: The Prince swept their left; Jinglong's troops then wheeled out behind the Prince's rear, and a great battle lasted long while arrows fell like rain.
idiomatic: The Prince rolled up their left; Li Jinglong's men curled behind him, and the fight dragged on under a rain of arrows.

literal: The Prince changed horses three times; when his arrows were spent he swung his sword; the blade broke and he ran up an embankment, feigning to raise his whip as though summoning followers behind.
idiomatic: Three horses fell under him; when his quiver was empty he hacked with his sword until the blade snapped; he scrambled onto a dike and flicked his whip as if calling up reserves.

literal: Jinglong suspected an ambush and dared not advance; Gaoxu came to the rescue, and the danger passed.
idiomatic: Li Jinglong feared a trap and held back; Zhu Gaoxu arrived in time and the Prince was saved.

literal: At that time the southern army was gathering ever thicker; the Yan officers and soldiers all turned pale.
idiomatic: More southern troops poured in by the hour, and the Yan ranks went grey with fear.

literal: The Prince said with spirit: "If I do not advance, the enemy will not retreat — there is nothing but to fight."
idiomatic: The Prince roused them: "Stand still and they will not leave — there is only to fight."

literal: He then again sent crack troops to burst out behind them and attacked from both sides.
idiomatic: He threw fresh shock troops through their rear and closed from both sides.

literal: A whirlwind arose, snapping Jinglong's banners; the Prince rode the wind, set fires, and struck fiercely; heads taken numbered in the tens of thousands, and those drowned exceeded one hundred thousand.
idiomatic: A whirlwind snapped Li Jinglong's standards; the Prince rode the gust, fired the field, and cut deep — tens of thousands slain and more than a hundred thousand drowned.

literal: Guo Ying broke west; Jinglong broke south; they lost entirely the imperial seals, writs, axes, and halberds they had been granted, and fled to Dezhou.
idiomatic: Guo Ying fled west, Li Jinglong south, abandoning the seals, commissions, axes, and halberds the throne had bestowed, and ran for Dezhou.

literal: In the fifth month, on the day guiyou, the Prince entered Dezhou; Jinglong fled to Jinan.
idiomatic: In the fifth month, on guiyou, the Prince entered Dezhou; Li Jinglong escaped to Jinan.

literal: On the day gengchen he attacked Jinan and defeated Jinglong's army below the walls.
idiomatic: On gengchen he assaulted Jinan and broke Li Jinglong's force beneath the walls.

literal: Tie Xuan and Sheng Yong held firm; the city could not be taken.
idiomatic: Tie Xuan and Sheng Yong held fast, and the city would not fall.

literal: In the eighth month, on the day wushen, he raised the siege and returned to Beiping.
idiomatic: In the eighth month, on wushen, he lifted the siege and returned to Beiping.

literal: In the ninth month Sheng Yong replaced Li Jinglong in command, retook Dezhou, and with Wu Jie, Ping An, and Xu Kai formed a pincer to hem in Beiping.
idiomatic: In the ninth month Sheng Yong took command from Li Jinglong, recovered Dezhou, and with Wu Jie, Ping An, and Xu Kai set a pincer meant to choke Beiping.

literal: At that time Xu Kai was investing Cangzhou; the Prince feigned a march on Liaodong, reached Tongzhou, followed the river south, crossed Zhigu, and marched day and night without rest.
idiomatic: Xu Kai was then besieging Cangzhou; the Prince pretended a strike into Liaodong, reached Tongzhou, turned south along the canal, crossed Zhigu, and drove without pause day or night.

literal: In the tenth month of winter, on the day wuwu, he surprised and seized Xu Kai, broke his city, and that night buried alive three thousand surrendered soldiers.
idiomatic: On wuwu in the tenth month he sprang on Xu Kai, stormed Cangzhou, and that night buried three thousand captives alive.

literal: He then crossed the river and passed Dezhou.
idiomatic: He forded on and passed Dezhou.

literal: Sheng Yong sent troops to strike him; he defeated them.
idiomatic: Sheng Yong sent a column against him; the Prince beat it off.

literal: In the eleventh month, on the day renshen, he reached Linqing.
idiomatic: In the eleventh month, on renshen, he reached Linqing.

literal: In the twelfth month, on the day dingyou, he surprised and broke Sheng Yong's general Sun Lin at Huakou.
idiomatic: In the twelfth month, on dingyou, he surprised Sheng Yong's general Sun Lin at Huakou and shattered him.

literal: On the day yimao he fought Yong at Dongchang; Yong with fire weapons and powerful crossbows annihilated the Prince's troops.
idiomatic: On yimao he met Sheng Yong at Dongchang; fire weapons and heavy crossbows cut the Prince's men to pieces.

literal: Ping An's army arrived; they surrounded him in many rings; the Prince was utterly defeated, broke out of the encirclement and escaped, losing tens of thousands; Zhang Yu died in battle.
idiomatic: Ping An came up and ringed him in layer after layer; the Prince suffered a crushing defeat, hacked his way out, left tens of thousands dead on the field, and Zhang Yu fell fighting.

literal: In the first month of the third year, on the day xinyou, he defeated Wu Jie and Ping An at Wei County and again at Shenzhou, then returned to Beiping.
idiomatic: In the first month of year 3, on xinyou, he routed Wu Jie and Ping An at Wei County and again at Shenzhou, then withdrew to Beiping.

literal: In the second month, on the day yisi, he again led his army south.
idiomatic: In the second month, on yisi, he marched south once more.

literal: In the third month, on the day xinsi, he met Sheng Yong at Jiahe; Tan Yuan died in battle.
idiomatic: In the third month, on xinsi, he clashed with Sheng Yong at Jiahe; Tan Yuan was killed.

literal: Zhu Neng and Zhang Wu fought to the death; Yong's army fell back slightly.
idiomatic: Zhu Neng and Zhang Wu fought as if each man were the last; Sheng Yong's line bent back a little.

literal: At dusk each side gathered its troops into camp.
idiomatic: At dusk both sides drew into camp.

literal: The Prince with a little more than ten horsemen pressed close to Yong's camp and slept in the open; when dawn came he looked about and found himself already within the encirclement.
idiomatic: The Prince camped with barely a dozen riders under Sheng Yong's very sentries; at dawn he woke surrounded.

literal: He then calmly led his horse, sounded the horn, and rode through the camp and out.
idiomatic: He simply walked his mount, blew his horn, and rode through the enemy lines and away.

literal: The generals, because the Son of Heaven had an edict that they must not earn the name of killing their uncle, stared at one another in alarm and hesitation and dared not loose a single arrow.
idiomatic: The southern commanders, bound by the Son of Heaven's order not to bear the guilt of slaying their uncle, gaped at one another and would not draw a bow.

literal: That day they fought again; from the hour chen to the hour wei the two armies traded victories; a northeast wind suddenly rose, dust blotted out the sky, the Yan troops shouted, and riding the wind they struck with fire; Yong was utterly defeated.
idiomatic: They fought again from chen to wei with neither side gaining; then a northeast gale blew up, dust swallowed the field, the Yan men roared, and charging with flame they broke Sheng Yong completely.

literal: He fled to Dezhou.
idiomatic: Sheng Yong fled to Dezhou.

literal: Wu Jie and Ping An led their armies from Zhending to join Yong; before they had gone eighty li they heard of the defeat and turned back.
idiomatic: Wu Jie and Ping An marched from Zhending to meet Sheng Yong; eighty li short of him they heard of the rout and turned back.

literal: The Prince lured them by stratagem; Jie and An led their troops out to surprise the Prince.
idiomatic: The Prince baited them; Wu Jie and Ping An sallied to ambush him.

literal: In the intercalary month, on the day wuxu, they met at Gaocheng.
idiomatic: In the intercalary month, on wuxu, the armies met at Gaocheng.
